R5B-bear-atv-0004.name: 460 m NW of Seymour River
R5B-bear-atv-0004.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R5B-bear-atv-0004.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Saghalie FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2012 (14 years old), 220 m W: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SE facing slope, 15 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 80 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Stuie, about 172 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 51.23108, -126.63538, where the truck road ends (Saghalie FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 2.2 km on unnamed roads and trails by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 20 m N, climb about 0 m.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 1-14, Region 1. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
